title: Machine-readable result transport still requires host JSON
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, the family-check path's CheckResult policy projection, bounded run_id plus per-test lineage digests, per-test canonical execution/observation JSON construction for ordinary bounded string/null fields, and bounded ArtifactStore payload/file digests are MNCS-owned. Python still supervises processes, projects typed values and raw diagnostics, constructs canonical run_id JSON, serializes TestResult/CheckResult JSON, and performs filesystem access; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries.
why_insufficient: The CheckResult, lineage-identity, and result-identity applications use shared MNCS JSON and SHA-256 capabilities, but the complete cross-repository evidence protocol, run_id JSON construction, and public result serialization are not yet application-level MNCS surfaces. Per-test lineage construction accepts up to 16 rows with 16,384 aggregate input bytes and fixed UTF-8 field limits; unusual value types or over-bound fields keep the compatibility path. Native digest work remains bounded by the toolchain's 8,000,000-step application ceiling. Large file/provenance hashes remain streamed through the host boundary. Python reassembles UTF-8-safe chunks where native byte fields are bounded to 1,024 bytes.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::make_result keeps canonical run_id JSON in Python and hashes it through test-result-identity; it sends ordinary per-test index/run/test-case/status/verdict fields to test-lineage-identity, which constructs and hashes canonical execution/observation JSON. Out-of-contract lineage values use the previous compact-JSON hash path. ArtifactStore.write, ArtifactStore.record_existing, and execute_entry use test-result-identity for bounded artifact content; tools/mncs_test.py::check_result calls test-check-result-projection, then serializes the typed native result as mncs.check-result/1 JSON.
desired_direction: A versioned native serialization/protocol library for bounded structured results, with explicit text/bytes policy and lossless adapter projections.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction; test-lineage-identity constructs and hashes ordinary per-test execution/observation JSON; and test-result-identity computes bounded run_id and ArtifactStore digests with mncs.std.sha256.v1. The adapter respects native row, field, payload, chunk, byte, and step limits; unusual or over-bound lineage values retain the exact compact-JSON compatibility path, individual over-budget content hashes retain the host fallback, and larger files are hashed as a stream. Python still constructs canonical run_id JSON, reassembles unresolved-message chunks, performs filesystem access, and serializes public JSON/artifacts. Python also retains process supervision, typed-value projection, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport; it no longer classifies subprocess transport or decoded execution outcomes.
